A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MetaDesigner. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original WordArt experiments, an 11-participant user study, SSIM/LPIPS comparisons, component analyses, and dataset and usage analytics.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds controls, VLM ratings, qualitative component comparisons, and GPT-4/GPT-4V selection results.

M1.justification: The four-agent pipeline, glyph generation, ToT selection from 68 LoRA models, ControlNet rendering, and feedback procedure remain unchanged. Equations 1–13 and Algorithm 1 retain their substance; the additional experimental variants do not establish a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate multilingual WordArt across English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and the same broad artistic domains. The additional examples and 25-prompt component study remain within this coverage; they change sampling and analysis rather than task requirements or language coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add SDXL-Aug and a MetaDesigner control captioned as without feedback. Table 3 and Figure 17 include a variant described as without agents, while Figure 19 and Appendix E add GPT-4V component comparisons. These additions substantially expand the controls beyond the retained original comparators.

E3.justification: Table 1 separates the previous combined Aesthetics & Creativity outcome into two outcomes. Table 3 introduces VLM aesthetics/creativity scoring on a 0–10 scale, and Appendix E introduces a 25-prompt model-selection evaluation. The original 150 prompts, 20 user-study prompts, 11 participants, and SSIM/LPIPS metrics remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ToT, LoRA-weight, and iterative-refinement analyses, v3 adds feedback/agent controls, merged versus separate glyph and texture design (Figure 18), evaluator comparisons (Figure 19), font effects (Figure 22), and GPT-4/GPT-4V selection analysis (Appendix E). These test additional central design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Table 4 counts selections across distinct prompts; it does not introduce repeated trials or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the user-study results, including MetaDesigner text accuracy changing from 93.8 to 96.8, alongside revised outcomes and comparators. This does not establish a same-setting performance gain. Shared Table 2 scores remain unchanged, while new control columns, Tables 3–4, and appendix figures substantially expand the reported results.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations 1–13 retain the same definitions and operations. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and v3 adds no substantive mathematical derivation or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain personalized multilingual WordArt through agents and feedback, a 68-model LoRA library, and a multilingual dataset exceeding 5,000 images. The updated visit count and additional evidence do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds difficulty with OCR as a rationale for human evaluation. Appendix E interprets GPT-4V's varied selections as better understanding of user intent and claims greater consistency for Future Technology, although Table 4 shows identical selections for both models in that category.

D1.justification: Appendix E supplies all 25 test prompts, and Figures 20–21 document a concrete pipeline example and interface controls. Existing algorithm, model-library, and prompt-template information is largely retained. The added SDXL-Aug and ablation configurations receive little implementation detail.

R1.justification: v3 removes the citations and bibliography entries for He et al.'s WordArt Designer and WordArt Designer API. The remaining related-work coverage and positioning around an interactive multi-agent framework are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and much of the method exposition are extensively rewritten with additional subheadings and structured explanations. Appendix B's walkthrough is condensed, and the standalone WordArt Dataset subsection disappears while its substantive description remains elsewhere.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 are expanded, Tables 3–4 and Figures 17–23 are added, and existing figures are resized and rearranged. The gallery moves from v1 Figure 14 in the appendix to v3 Figure 9 in the main text. Conference formatting also changes headers, typography, and spacing.

improvement.justification: The added quantitative feedback controls and glyph/texture separation comparison strengthen evidence for design choices that v1 supported less directly. Clearer exposition and explicit test prompts also help. Gains are limited by sparse configuration details, inconsistent meanings of Ours*, an unsupported interpretation in Appendix E, and removal of the closely related WordArt Designer citations.
